name: AI Ear Training
description: AI terms and one-line concepts, built for repeated exposure
prompt: Use AI terms precisely; on first mention you may add the Chinese equivalent. Avoid name-dropping.

long: A model doesn't memorize answers. It memorizes a probability map of what tends to come next.
Attention, plainly: every token gets to ask who in the room is relevant to me.
Overfitting isn't learning too well. It's memorizing the answer key, including the handwriting.
Temperature zero gives you a very obedient, very boring colleague.
Hallucination isn't lying. It's filling a gap it can't see, in its most confident voice.
RAG is an open-book exam: no one expects you to memorize it, just to know where to look.
Gradient descent is walking downhill. Learning rate decides whether you step or bounce.
The annoying thing about scaling laws: they work, and nobody can quite say why.
Alignment doesn't make a model smarter. It stops it from applying smarts somewhere strange.
Distillation compresses an old professor's intuition into a crib sheet for undergrads.
Backprop is just asking, all the way back, who should be blamed for this error.
Embeddings mean words with similar meanings end up living near each other.
A token is neither a word nor a character. It's a fragment the model found convenient.
The context window is a desk. However big, some files still won't fit.
Chain of thought isn't thinking. It's writing the intermediate steps where they can be seen.
KV cache is inference's notebook: keys and values already computed shouldn't be computed twice.
Quantization moves weights into a smaller house. Give up a little precision, gain a lot of speed.
LoRA's trick: leave the big model alone, tape a small trainable note beside it.
Catastrophic forgetting: learn the new task, lose the old one completely.
Reward hacking: every metric is green and nothing got done.
Emergent abilities sound mystical, until you notice we picked a ruler that only jumps at that scale.
MoE is a consultation: wake only the relevant experts, let the rest keep sleeping.
Diffusion models first learn to turn photos into noise, then learn to run that backwards.
Lower perplexity means fewer surprises about the next token. Fewer surprises, smoother sentences.
An agent is a model with a to-do list and a set of keys it's actually allowed to use.
Prompt injection isn't a hack. It's someone whispering in the model's ear pretending to be the boss.
Context rot: pile in enough material and the model walks right past the one page that mattered.
Lost in the middle: long documents lose their middle. The ends it remembers fine.
Speculative decoding has a junior take a guess; the senior stamps it if right, does it themselves if not.
Prefix caching computes the same opening line once, like memorizing your own introduction.
Continuous batching is a carpool: whoever shows up boards, nobody waits for a full van.
Tensor parallelism splits one big block across several hands, then reconciles the totals.
FSDP is a shared flat: everyone has a room, and the living room wall comes down when needed.
Pruning gives the network a haircut. The hair doesn't do the thinking anyway.
Model merging averages two speciallists' answers and somehow beats both on the exam.
Model routing is triage: easy cases to the intern, hard ones to the attending.
A golden set isn't the answer key. It's the batch of samples you're willing to argue about.
LLM judges fail like human judges: they favor long, polished, and whichever came first.
pass@k means: give it k attempts and one of them will eventually land.
Differential privacy salts the data. The statistics still taste right; no individual can be picked out.
Model watermarking presses a pattern into the paper, invisible until you hold it to the light.
Data poisoning is quietly editing one worked example in the textbook. Everyone fails on exam day.
Synthetic data is the model eating what it produced: nourishing if done well, malnourishing if not.
Data mixture is a recipe. Same ingredients, wrong ratios, a different dish entirely.
Curriculum learning orders the textbook by difficulty: arithmetic before calculus.
Early stopping is tapping it on the shoulder right before it starts rote memorizing.
Weight decay charges rent on parameters. Rooms occupied too long get emptied out.
Gradient clipping ties a rope to a runaway update and pulls it back when it drifts.
Warmup is easing off the clutch before the gas, so the engine doesn't stall.
Mixed precision is scratch paper for the middle steps, careful handwriting only at the end.
Gradient checkpointing trades time for memory: store nothing, recompute when needed.
FlashAttention didn't invent new math. It just stopped moving data around so much.
Grouped-query attention shares one memory across several heads: half the bandwidth, barely less wit.
A causal mask means no peeking ahead. You can only see the part already written.
A residual connection installs an elevator so gradients don't have to climb every floor.
Layer norm sets every floor to the same volume, so it doesn't get louder as you go up.
SwiGLU is the little valve in the feedforward layer: softer than ReLU, and it works better.
Expert routing is a bouncer. One call goes out, and only the experts on shift get in.
Mamba replaces full attention with a recurrence, turning quadratic cost into linear.
A vision encoder cuts the image into tiles and reads them as tokens: pictures become sentences.
Native multimodality is one brain seeing and hearing directly, not translating to text first.
Constitutional AI hands it a rulebook, then lets it audit itself against the rulebook.
DPO skips the reward model and tunes directly on 'this is better than that' preferences.
GRPO lets a group of answers compete; whoever leads the group gets the reward, no separate judge.
Rejection sampling casts a wide net and keeps only the good ones. Expensive, but simple.
A process reward model watches the steps. An outcome model only sees the finish line — cheaper, easier to game.
Test-time compute: rather than train a stronger model, let the one you have think longer.
Long thinking isn't hesitation. It's spending the reasoning budget on the genuinely hard steps.
Self-consistency has it answer ten times and vote. The majority usually beats the first try.
MCTS tries paths repeatedly, exploring more where the odds of winning look better.
A reflection loop is reading your own draft and backing up a step when it's wrong.
ReAct is think-act-observe: reason a step, take an action, look at the result, reason again.
MCP is a plug standard for tools. Anyone can plug in; no custom wiring per tool.
Sandboxed execution puts it in a cage first. If something breaks, nothing outside gets hit.
Guardrails aren't walls. They're the sieve at the exit that catches what shouldn't leave.
Hybrid retrieval combines keyword precision with vector breadth: miss nothing, skew nothing.
Reranking is skimming a wide pile, then reading the few likeliest closely.
Chunk overlap leaves a margin between pages so the key sentence never lands in the seam.
HNSW builds a highway network for vectors: fast roads first, then narrow alleys.
A semantic cache says 'I've answered something close to this' and skips the inference.
Chinchilla-optimal says stop stacking parameters and grow the data alongside them.
Double descent is counterintuitive: past a certain size, test error falls again instead of rising.
Grokking is a model that memorized early and only much later actually understood.
The lottery ticket hypothesis says a winning subnet hides inside a big net; training merely finds it.
Superposition is one neuron moonlighting in several meanings, crowded but still separable.
A sparse autoencoder decants the perfume: separates the blended scent into single notes.
Interpretability isn't the model proving its innocence. It's us finding the wire it's actually using.
In-context learning: never trained on it, but give it three examples and it picks up the format.
Few-shot prompting is handing over two worked examples instead of a half-hour of rules.
The system prompt is a boot setting: invisible to the user, decisive for the day's mood.
Jailbreaking isn't breaking in. It's going around: rephrase until it opens the door itself.
Red teaming is inviting people to dismantle your own work. The harder they try, the safer launch.
Membership inference asks 'have you seen this record?' and reads the confidence in the answer.
PII redaction swaps names and numbers for placeholders before the data ever reaches the model.
Data cleaning sets the ceiling more than architecture does. Garbage in, garbage out, guaranteed.
Self-play is shadowboxing: whichever hand wins keeps the lesson.
BLEU counts overlapping words, not meaning. A high score isn't a good translation.
MMLU tests breadth. HumanEval tests whether the code it writes actually runs.
The danger in A/B evaluation isn't noise. It's testing only the side you wanted to see.
Cost per million tokens is the real product metric. Capability you can't afford is capability you don't have.
An inference engine squeezes the paper FLOPs dry — several times the throughput, not one weight changed.
GGUF packs a model into a box you can carry; suddenly a laptop is enough.
AWQ and GPTQ both guess which weights don't matter. Guess right and quantization costs almost nothing.
Embedding dimension is the address length per concept: too short to fit, too long and it's mostly empty rooms.
High attention entropy means it's still deciding where to look. Low means it has locked on.
The logit distribution is every hesitation the model has in the instant before it speaks.
Vocabulary size trades granularity against memory: finer cuts save tokens and cost parameters.
Structured output isn't the model behaving. It's the sampler narrowed to the only legal paths.
Time to first token decides whether it feels fast; throughput decides whether the bill stays small. They usually fight.
Sequence packing stuffs the trunk: fill each batch so memory isn't dragged down by the shortest sequence.
The nastiest thing about contamination: you can't tell whether it remembered or already knew.
Long-term memory isn't storing every transcript. It's knowing which page you'll reopen.
Multi-agent isn't more heads, more speed. Without clear roles, the meeting is slower than the work.
Prompt tuning changes no weights at all. It hangs a clearer sign at the door.
An attention sink is the empty seat a model always keeps, for when nothing else is worth looking at.
